==English== {{wp|,+ing}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:loken|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|loken}}, {{m|enm|lokien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lōcian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lōkōn}}. Further origin {{unk|en|title=unknown}}, no certain cognates outside Germanic.{{R:Philippa EWN 2009|look}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|luke}}, {{m|sco|luik}}, {{m|sco|leuk|t=to look, see}}, {{cog|fy|lôkje}}, {{m|fy|loaitsje|t=to look}}, {{cog|nl|loeken|t=to look}}, {{cog|nds-de|löken}}. Likely also related to {{cog|de|lugen|t=to peek}}, {{cog|gsw|luege|t=to look}}, {{cog|yi|לוגן}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|lo͝ok}}, {{IPA|en|/lʊk/}} ** {{IPA|en|[lɵk]|a=SSB}} *** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-look.wav|a=Southern England|IPA=[lɵk]}} ** {{homophones|en|luck>>}} * {{IPA|en|/luːk/> dialects, esp. Bolton, <>>}} {{q|formerly more widespread}}{{R:Critical Pronouncing Dictionary|Look|351|2|ipage=1}} ** {{IPA|en|[lʉːx]> variant>}} ** {{homophones|en|Luke}} * {{IPA|en|/lʉk/|a=Scotland,Northern Ireland}} ** {{homophones|en|Luke}} * {{rhymes|en|ʊk|uːk|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # To [[try]] to [[see]], to [[pay attention]] to with one’s [[eyes]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:look}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} {{non-gloss|As an intransitive verb, often with "at".}} ##: {{troponyms|en|glance|Thesaurus:stare}} ##: {{ux|en|They kept '''looking''' at me.}} ##: {{ux|en|Don’t '''look''' in the closet.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=Then came a maid with hand-bag and shawls, and after her a tall young lady.{{...}}She '''looked''' around expectantly, and recognizing Mrs. Cooke's maid{{...}}Miss Thorn greeted her with a smile which greatly prepossessed us in her favor.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=10|passage=He '''looked''' round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the bad engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his own.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} {{non-gloss|As a transitive verb, often in the {{glossary|imperative mood|imperative}}; chiefly takes {{glossary|relative clause}} as direct object.}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Look''' what you did to him!}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Look''' who's back!}} # {{senseid|en|appear}} To [[appear]], to [[seem]]. #: {{ux|en|It '''looks''' as if it’s going to rain soon. ''or'' It '''looks''' like it’s going to rain soon. ''or'' It looks like rain [is coming].}} #: {{ux|en|Our new boss '''looks''' to be friendly.}} #: {{ux|en|It '''looks''' as if [''or'' like] I'm stuck with you.}} #: {{ux|en|{{q|UK}} He always '''looks''' like scoring a goal if not two.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1701-03|author=w:Joseph Addison|url=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=HoUTAAAAQAAJ|title=Remarks on Several Parts of Italy, &c.|publisher=Dedication |passage=THERE is a pleaſure in owning obligations which it is a pleaſure to have received; but ſhould I publiſh any favours done me by your Lordſhip, I am afraid it would '''look''' more like vanity, than gratitude.}} #* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|IV |passage=So this was my future home, I thought!{{...}}Backed by towering hills, the but faintly discernible purple line of the French boundary off to the southwest, a sky of palest Gobelin flecked with fat, fleecy little clouds, it in truth '''looked''' a dear little city; the city of one's dreams.}} #* {{RQ:Williams Velveteen Rabbit|passage=He loved him so hard that he loved all his whiskers off, and the pink lining to his ears turned grey, and his brown spots faded. He even began to lose his shape, and he scarcely '''looked''' like a rabbit any more, except to the Boy.}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=2|passage=Now that she had rested and had fed from the luncheon tray Mrs. Broome had just removed, she had reverted to her normal gaiety.  She '''looked''' cool in a grey tailored cotton dress with a terracotta scarf and shoes and her hair a black silk helmet.}} #* {{quote-web|en|year=2012|title=Chelsea 6-0 Wolves|site=bbc.co.uk|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19632463 |passage=Chelsea's youngsters, who '''looked''' lively throughout, then combined for the second goal in the seventh minute. Romeu's shot was saved by Wolves goalkeeper Dorus De Vries but Piazon kept the ball alive and turned it back for an unmarked Bertrand to blast home.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=52| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/21579039-chinas-growing-empire-ports-abroad-mainly-about-trade-not-aggression-new-masters The new masters and commanders]| passage=From the ground, Colombo’s port does not '''look''' like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the port after lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.}} # {{lb|en|copulative}} To give an appearance of being. #: {{ux|en|What a fright you '''looked''' in that hideous outfit.}} #: {{ux|en|That painting '''looks''' nice.}} #: {{ux|en|You’re '''looking''' worried. Whaddya thinking about?}} #: {{ux|en|You '''looked''' a fool when you slipped on a banana peel.}} #: {{ux|en|You didn't use to '''look''' so dismal, but now you '''look'''/are '''look'''ing positively unhappy.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1843|author=w:Thomas Carlyle|title=[[:w:Past and Present (book)|Past and Present]]|section=book 2, chapter 6, ''Monk Samson''|passage=Once, slipping the money clandestinely, just in the act of taking leave, he slipt it not into her hand but on the floor, and another had it; whereupon the poor Monk, coming to know it, '''looked''' mere despair for some days{{nb...}}.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|often|with "for"}} To [[search]] for, to [[try]] to [[find]]. # To face or present a view. #: {{ux|en|The hotel '''looks''' over the valleys of the Hindu Kush.}} #* '''1769''', {{w|Benjamin Blayney}} (editor), ''{{w|King James Version|King James Bible}}'', Oxford standard text, ''[[s:Bible (King James)/Ezekiel|Ezekiel]]'', xi, 1, #* {{RQ:Dunsany Pegana |passage=Wornath-Mavai lieth in a valley and '''looketh''' towards the south, and on the slopes of it Sish rested among the flowers when Sish was young.}} # To expect or anticipate. #: {{ux|en|I '''look''' to each hour for my lover’s arrival.}} #* '''1596''', {{w|Edmund Spenser}}, ''{{w|The Fairie Queene}}'', Book VI, Canto XI, '''1750''', ''The Works of Edmund Spenser'', Volume 4, [https://books.google.com.au/books?id=PyxMAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA139&dq=%22looking+each+hour+into+death%27s+mouth+to+fall%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjTjumR2vLZAhVSOZAKHTDnBAMQ6AEIJzAA#v=onepage&q=%22looking%20each%20hour%20into%20death's%20mouth%20to%20fall%22&f=false page 139], #* {{RQ:Noire Thug-A-Licious|page=108|passage="Ain't gone be no Rikers Island for you next time," I warned him. '''Looking''' each Hour into Death's Mouth to fall,}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-1|1|1|passage=Gloster, what ere we like, thou art Protector,
And '''lookest''' to command the Prince and Realme.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[express]] or [[manifest]] by a look. #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1815|author=w:Lord Byron|title=Waterloo |passage=Soft eyes '''looked''' love to eyes which spake again,}} #* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage=For a few seconds Mr Carlyle '''looked''' his unutterable feelings. When he did speak it was with crushing deliberation.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|year_published=1959|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Moonraker (novel)|Moonraker}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter=The Columbite King|page=13|passage="Still sunburned, I see." M. '''looked''' his disapproval. He didn't really begrudge Bond a holiday which had been partly convalescence. The hint of criticism came from the Puritan and the Jesuit who live in all leaders of men.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|often|with "to"}} To make sure of, to see to. #* {{RQ:Homer Butler Odyssey|passage="'''Look''' to it yourself, father," answered Telemachus, "for they say you are the wisest counsellor in the world, and that there is no other mortal man who can compare with you.{{nb...}}}} # {{lb|en|dated|sometimes|figurative}} To show oneself in looking; to [[peep out]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|Induction|2|text=I have{{...}}more feet than shoes, or such shoes as my toes '''look''' through the overleather.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|archaic|_|or|_|dialectal}} To [[check#Verb|check]], to [[make sure#Verb|make sure]] (of something). #* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=II|page=151|passage=Finding it was like to overblow, we took in our Sprit-ſail, and ſtood by to hand the Fore-ſail;
